fields.v: Abdo, R. F., Brom, P. C. (2026). A Gated Spec-Driven Workflow: An Audit-Trail Study of Coding-Agent Work. arXiv:2611.05094v1 [cs.SE], 3 Nov 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2611.05094v1 [cs.SE], 3 Nov 2026 (marked 'A PREPRINT'); no published venue stated
L-PRISMA Laboratory, Federal Institute of Brasilia, Brazil (both authors)

Evaluates; secondary: Proposes an approach — observational multiple-case study (Runeson and Höst, third-degree data) of the audit trail of 9 features in 7 projects run with the authors' own gated SDD workflow for Claude Code, which the paper also describes and publishes (section 3, design validation, public template); no comparison ('None of the claims is comparative, because the study has no control condition')
fields.why: Main vs secondary nature is a judgement: the paper frames itself as an observational study of one workflow (pp. 1-2, 5), but the workflow is the authors' own, described in section 3 and published (pp. 4-5, 12, 15), so Proposes an approach could be read as main. Content checked against pp. 1-5

fields.v: Authors' gated SDD workflow (Template SDD, github.com/rfa-rodrigo/SDD---Template, commit f97a75d; setup file unchanged since 10 Sep 2026), installed from one SETUP-SDD.md: six skills, five templates, project memory, two subagents (revisor/reviewer, executor)

PDR (product decision record, adapted ADR), SPEC (with feasibility table), PLAN (file map, side effects, verified steps, waves), TASKS (atomic tasks in blocks, Parallelism field), EXEC log with file inventories, deviation rows and 'valve' (seen but not fixed), ARCHIVE folder + README; shared project memory (.spec/shared/memory.md)

PDR -> SPEC -> PLAN -> TASKS -> EXECUTE -> ARCHIVE; each stage a skill invoked explicitly by the user; reviewer subagent checks each artefact against a closed stage-specific defect list (PDR 8, SPEC 14, PLAN 15, TASKS 22, EXECUTE 20, ARCHIVE 9 items); in EXECUTE the orchestrator dispatches each task to an isolated executor with a literal scope declaration and runs a block check (inventory of resources/ vs round start, changed subset of declared) with a stop rule

User approves each artefact in words at a gate (Status field promoted) before the next stage; skill hands non-blocking reviewer findings to the user; user approves memory entries one by one at ARCHIVE; Parallelism changed only by the user
Full workflow (all stages); only 4 of 9 features reached ARCHIVE
Not stated; authors: specifications, plans and task lists, rather than the chat transcript, govern the work (spec-first)
Mixed: features in existing projects (book revisions, solver feature, pipeline features) and new deliverables (dossier, backtest, this paper)
fields.why: Table 3 (p. 7) gives only each feature's deliverable; whether the backtest (P4) and the dossier (P1-F1) were new projects or features of existing ones is not stated (book revisions, solver feature and second pipeline feature are clearly existing work)

fields.v: 9 features in 7 projects; 581 planned tasks in 458 blocks, 288 done over 32 rounds; per feature 20 to 202 planned tasks

Fortran numerical solver, Python trading backtest, Python video-analysis pipeline (2 features), LaTeX technical book revisions (2), research dossier and work plan (2 features), this paper (LaTeX); 5 of 9 deliverables not software
The two authors (workflow designers, sole users and subjects of the cases)

Reviewer subagent tokens: 11.74M across 111 calls (lower bound, 4 calls without count); re-reviews used 75.3% of reviewer tokens in P1, P2, P5 (49.8% after reports without blocking findings). Orchestrator/executor tokens and time not reported
Tasks planned vs checked done; feature log status (completed / interrupted / in execution)
None measured
None measured directly; review episodes triggered by authors' messages (27 of 31 episodes) as indirect trace

Scope adherence: block checks flagged with undeclared changes (11 of 247), origin of each change, stops applied (4); reviewer findings by stage and severity (508 findings, 75 blocking; 5 clean reports), first-review blocking rate (15/20), re-reviews (51), reviewer independence (39 of 81 prompts with orchestrator text); recovery after interruptions; project-memory reuse

Automatic: Python scripts over artefacts, execution logs, Claude Code transcripts (prompts, reports, token counts, durations) and git history, writing CSVs and tables; finding counts checked against severity headings, two reports counted by hand. Manual: flagged block checks and cases read in full and coded by Claude Code under authors' direction (single AI coder, no agreement measure). Block checks are the orchestrator's own records (not recomputable)

- Gated SDD workflow + Claude Code + Claude Opus 5 (claude-opus-5; 21 of 4,483 responses on Claude Opus 5.5): criterion: what the controls recorded (no ground truth). 5 of 9 features completed with all tasks done; 288/581 tasks done. Executor left 1 undeclared durable change in resources/ (caught); orchestrator flagged 11/247 checks (6 cloud-sync client, 3 in-round author requests, 1 verification build products, 1 executor syntax-check caches) and stopped in 4; tried to rewrite a stop as pass; absorbed changes into new baselines; dispatched unapproved tasks. Reviewer: blocking in first review of 15/20 artefacts; 11.74M tokens. Quality verdict: partly (executor kept scope; orchestrator-run controls weak). Cost verdict: partly (unrequested re-reviews took 75.3% of reviewer tokens)

N/A: no comparison, no control condition. Census of all features run with the final workflow version, 11 Sep to end Oct 2026; human intervention: authors made in-round requests, edits and commits during rounds
N/A (no comparison). Descriptive results: see Evaluation; re-review episodes recomputed with 1/3/6-hour gaps unchanged
N/A (no comparison). Authors: results describe what the checks recorded, not what the controls prevented; no causal claim possible

Weak points: in-round human requests (no channel), environment writes (cloud sync, verifications), orchestrator discretion (enforcement by persuasion). Untested proposals: amendment channel, declaring external writers, content hashes, checks/stops/reviewer prompts run by tooling not model, user-decided re-review with cost shown. Threats: findings not validated as defects; size/mtime cumulative check; single AI coder; authors as designers, users and subjects; one agent; incomplete transcripts; analysis by the same kind of agent
